reflections.title: "To Overlook an Offense"

reflect.text: When someone hurts or offends us, our first reaction is often anger. But true wisdom gives us the patience to pause and overlook personal slights. Instead of rushing to offer quick answers or defend ourselves, real patience begins when we use our ears. Listening attentively to another viewpoint shows that the person and their feelings genuinely matter to us.

Wisdom also gives us insight into what others may be carrying. When we take time to understand the painful circumstances behind a person's behavior, our hearts move toward empathy instead of anger. Trevin Wax points to Abraham Lincoln's gracious choice to let go of personal humiliation from Edwin Stanton as an example of this patience. Choosing forgiveness over a grudge can heal damaged friendships and unlock unexpected blessings. By patiently bearing with the weaknesses and frustrations of others, we quietly reflect Jesus.

questions: Is there an offense or unkind remark you need to overlook today instead of holding a grudge?
How can listening more carefully to someone who frustrates you help you show Christ's patience?
reflections.prayer: Lord, give us the wisdom and insight to be patient when others offend us. Help us to listen well, to understand their struggles, and to choose forgiveness over holding a grudge. Make us gentle and gracious so that our lives reflect Jesus to those around us. Amen.

reflections.title: "A Loan to the Lord"

reflect.text: When we help those in need, our motives matter. Charles Spurgeon reminds us to give out of pure sympathy and compassion, not to gain praise or win influence over people. We should never expect the poor to pay us back, or even to thank us. Instead, God invites us to view our kindness as something we are lending directly to Him. He steps in, takes on the debt Himself, and gives us His personal promise to repay.

F. B. Meyer notes that our world would change completely if we truly believed this truth. We often imagine that we only keep what we hold onto, but in God's kingdom, the safest investments are made by caring for the needy. God calls us to act as His faithful stewards, sharing His wealth with open hands. You can never outgive the Lord, because He will never remain in your debt. He notices every act of mercy and will faithfully repay you in His own time and way.

questions: When you give to someone in need, do you expect appreciation, or do you view it as giving directly to God?
How does knowing that the Lord promises to repay your kindness change the way you share what you have?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for trusting us to care for those in need around us. Cleanse our hearts of selfish motives and give us true compassion for the poor. Help us to give freely and joyfully, knowing that You see every gift and will never fail to keep Your promises. Amen.

reflections.title: "The Purpose of the Lord"

reflect.text: We often fill our hearts with ambitious goals and detailed plans for the future. Yet as human beings, our capacity, wisdom, and control are very limited. When we rely solely on our own understanding, unexpected changes quickly produce fear and anxiety. We need to remember that while we make many plans, only the sovereign purpose of the Lord endures. Unfulfilled dreams or interrupted schedules are not personal failures; they are often divine redirections guiding our lives toward God's will.

The early disciples experienced this when Jesus interrupted their everyday routines and called them to a higher purpose. Because God is completely holy, wise, and good, His ultimate control provides deep comfort for our souls. When sudden detours occur, we do not need to panic or lose hope. Trusting that the Lord's plans will prevail frees us from worry and allows us to find true rest in His loving care.

questions: How do you usually respond when your plans are suddenly interrupted or changed?
How does remembering God's goodness and wisdom bring you peace when life takes an unexpected turn?
reflections.prayer: Lord, we surrender our many plans and personal ambitions into Your hands today. When our lives are interrupted, help us see Your gentle redirection instead of feeling defeated. Give our souls peace and rest, knowing that Your wise and good purpose will always prevail. Amen.

D6.author: Christina Patterson
D6.work: Allow God’s Purpose To Interrupt Your Plans
